title: Laptop Design Comparison Showcase
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D laptop design comparison showcase using Three.js. Load the 'Michelle.glb' model using GLTFLoader as a human figure standing behind a product display table for scale reference.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a clean showroom environment with a light gray floor plane (50x50 units) and subtle gradient background (white to light blue).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and two directional lights: one from upper-left (intensity 0.8) and one from upper-right (intensity 0.6).
- Camera starts at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Load 'Michelle.glb' model, scale it to approximately 2 units tall, position at (0, 0, -2) behind the display area.

LAPTOP MODELS:
- Create TWO laptop models using Three.js geometry (boxes and planes):
  - Laptop A ("ProBook Ultra"): positioned at (-2, 1, 0). Base: box 2.4x0.08x1.6 (dark silver, metallic material). Screen: box 2.4x1.6x0.04 hinged at back edge of base. Screen displays a blue gradient plane.
  - Laptop B ("AirSlim Max"): positioned at (2, 1, 0). Base: box 2.2x0.05x1.4 (space gray, metallic material). Screen: box 2.2x1.4x0.03 hinged at back edge of base. Screen displays a green gradient plane.
- Both laptops sit on a display table (box 6x1x2, white material) centered at (0, 0.5, 0).
- Both laptops start with screens open at 110 degrees from the base.

INTERACTION - SELECTION:
- Clicking on a laptop (raycasting) selects it. Selected laptop gets a subtle golden emissive outline (emissive color #FFD700, intensity 0.3).
- Only one laptop can be selected at a time. Clicking empty space deselects all.

INTERACTION - SCREEN ANGLE:
- When a laptop is selected, pressing UP arrow opens the screen more (increase angle by 10 degrees, max 170 degrees).
- Pressing DOWN arrow closes the screen (decrease angle by 10 degrees, min 0 degrees = fully closed).
- The screen should rotate around the hinge (back edge of base).

INTERACTION - ROTATION:
- When a laptop is selected, pressing LEFT/RIGHT arrows rotates the entire laptop (base+screen) around its Y-axis by 15 degrees.

INTERACTION - COMPARISON MODE:
- Add a DOM button with id='btn-compare' labeled 'Compare Side by Side'. When clicked, both laptops animate smoothly (over 1 second) to move closer: Laptop A to (-1.5, 1, 1) and Laptop B to (1.5, 1, 1), both rotating to face the camera (Y rotation = 0).
- Add a DOM button with id='btn-reset' labeled 'Reset Positions'. When clicked, laptops animate back to original positions.

INTERACTION - SPECS PANEL:
- Add a DOM button with id='btn-specs' labeled 'Toggle Specs'. When clicked, show/hide a specs overlay panel (id='specs-panel') displaying:
  - ProBook Ultra: 15.6", 2.1kg, i7, 16GB RAM
  - AirSlim Max: 14", 1.3kg, M2, 8GB RAM

INTERACTION - COLOR VARIANT:
- Add a DOM button with id='btn-color' labeled 'Switch Color'. When clicked, cycle the selected laptop's base color through: silver (#C0C0C0), space gray (#4A4A4A), midnight blue (#191970). Track color index per laptop.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - selectedLaptop: null | 'A' | 'B'
  - laptopA_screenAngle: number (degrees, starts at 110)
  - laptopB_screenAngle: number (degrees, starts at 110)
  - laptopA_yRotation: number (degrees, starts at 0)
  - laptopB_yRotation: number (degrees, starts at 0)
  - compareMode: boolean (false initially)
  - specsVisible: boolean (false initially)
  - laptopA_colorIndex: number (0 initially)
  - laptopB_colorIndex: number (0 initially)
  - modelLoaded: boolean (false until Michelle.glb loads)
  - laptopA_position: {x, y, z}
  - laptopB_position: {x, y, z}

HUD:
- Display currently selected laptop name in a div with id='selection-label' at top-center. Show 'None Selected' when nothing is selected.
- All buttons should be styled with padding 10px 20px, positioned in a vertical toolbar on the right side of the screen.
physics_constraints: Screen angle must remain clamped between 0 and 170 degrees. Laptop Y-rotation wraps around at 360 degrees. Positions must not contain NaN values. Animations should use smooth interpolation (lerp or tween). Laptops must remain on the table surface (y >= 1).
